title: Quantum chemistry with the EigenVista connector

scenes.title: Connect to the released window
scenes.caption: Ask the agent to connect, protect unsaved work, and open approved input.
scenes.narration: Connect your external agent to a released EigenVista window using the setup instructions. Give it the session note and ask it to protect unsaved work. Open the supplied water calculation in the approved input folder. Check the three atoms and twenty-four imported orbitals before choosing a field.
scenes.prompt: Use my connected window. Keep unsaved work safe, open the approved water Molden file, and report its molecular and orbital counts.

scenes.title: Identify the HOMO from metadata
scenes.caption: Report the highest occupied and lowest zero-occupation orbital by energy.
scenes.narration: Ask the agent to read the energies and occupations in the source. For this closed-shell example, the highest occupied orbital is MO five and the lowest zero-occupation orbital is MO six. Use the returned field identity in the subsequent requests.
scenes.prompt: Find the highest-energy occupied orbital and the lowest-energy orbital with zero occupation. Include the IDs, energies, and units.

scenes.title: Review a preview before generating meshes
scenes.caption: Compare raycast and volume previews at 64 samples per axis.
scenes.narration: Ask for the sampled raycast preview and then the volume preview at sixty-four samples per axis. Keep the same camera and field. After each change, have the agent read back the display state. These sampled views let you decide whether to calculate a persistent mesh.
scenes.prompt: Preview the HOMO in raycast and volume modes at 64 samples per axis, with a fixed camera.

scenes.title: Publish the signed orbital figure
scenes.caption: Wait for the signed mesh pair and export a transparent PNG with the field key.
scenes.narration: Generate the signed pair at plus and minus zero point zero three. Ask the agent to wait for success, report the two mesh counts, and verify the exported PNG includes the signed field key. If a calculation needs to stop, identify that job specifically and confirm the prior completed result is still available.
scenes.prompt: Generate the HOMO mesh pair, verify completion and signed levels, then export a transparent PNG with its field key.

scenes.title: Verify the numerical profile
scenes.caption: Ask for 65 samples and a separate CSV for the bond measurement.
scenes.narration: Request a distance monitor for the oxygen and first hydrogen, then sample the same orbital along that segment. Check that the sixty-five rows include both endpoints. Compare the measured bond and profile length, and read the status and scalar unit columns before using the table elsewhere.
scenes.prompt: Measure the O–H bond and export a 65-point HOMO profile along that bond. Confirm the length and scalar units.

scenes.title: Inspect a different surface finish
scenes.caption: Apply clipping to an identified surface and record the shader values.
scenes.narration: After saving the orbital result, use a fresh copy to compare an electron-density shell and a solvent-accessible surface. Ask the agent to apply a clipping shader to an identified shell and return the exact parameter values with the figure.
scenes.prompt: Show the total density and solvent-accessible surfaces one at a time, then clip the density shell to reveal the molecule.

scenes.title: Keep reusable figures, tables and settings
scenes.caption: Verify the output files and preserve an editable native record.
scenes.narration: Ask the agent to check that every output opens from the results folder. Keep the PNG and tables with the original calculation, the camera and shader settings, and the native file. For batch conversion, use the bundled converter and verify each converted file separately.
scenes.prompt: Check the exported figure and tables, save an editable native document, and list the exact files and settings.
